s0204.literal: None of the plans was not participated in [by him]—[yan] supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0204.idiomatic: On "none of the plans was not participated in": yan supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

s0205.literal: His son Yun'gong succeeded—Hall edition verification says the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Yuan for Yun.
s0205.idiomatic: On "his son Yun'gong succeeded": the Hall edition notes the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Yuan for Yun.

s0206.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang [Chang], when he was Administrator of Wuxing—Chang was still young—[Chang] supplied according to Yuan Gui 708 and 727.
s0206.idiomatic: On "Prince Xian of Hengyang when Administrator of Wuxing, Chang still young": Chang supplied per Yuan Gui 708 and 727.

s0207.literal: Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies among the Twenty-two Histories says the character Chang should be moved to below Prince Xian of Hengyang.
s0207.idiomatic: Qian Daxin holds the character Chang should stand under Prince Xian of Hengyang.

s0208.literal: Present review: only a missing Chang under Prince Xian of Hengyang; the Chang below should not be moved.
s0208.idiomatic: Present review: only one Chang is missing after Prince Xian of Hengyang; the lower Chang should not be moved.

s0209.literal: Also received one hundred bolts of silk as gift from Ouyang Wuwei—Hall edition verification says the History of the Southern Dynasties lacks the character Wu.
s0209.idiomatic: On "also received one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei": the Hall edition notes the History of the Southern Dynasties omits Wu.

s0210.literal: Present review: this too changes a restored full name to a single name; the History of the Southern Dynasties often does so.
s0210.idiomatic: Present review: here too a full name is reduced to a single character, as the History of the Southern Dynasties often does.

s0211.literal: Concurrently Grand Boat Minister—"Grand Boat Minister" in the Southern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions all read Grand Storehouse Minister.
s0211.idiomatic: On "concurrently Grand Boat Minister": the Southern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions all read Grand Storehouse Minister.

s0212.literal: Hall edition verification says: "'fu' in the Supervisory edition was wrongly written 'zhou'; now corrected.
s0212.idiomatic: The Hall edition holds the Supervisory edition wrongly wrote zhou for fu and emended it—note:

s0213.literal: " Present review: In the seventh year of Liang Tianjian, the Commissioner of Waterways was made Grand Boat Minister, lowest among the regular ministers, overseeing boats and embankments—see the Treatise on Officials in the Book of Sui; the Hall edition wrongly emended.
s0213.idiomatic: Present review: in Liang Tianjian year 7 the commissioner of waterways became Grand Boat Minister, the lowest regular minister, in charge of shipping and dikes (Book of Sui, Treatise on Officials); the Hall emendation is wrong.

s0214.literal: Chief Administrator to the Prince of Changsha, Xuan-yi [style]—"Xuan-yi" in the Ji edition reads "Xuan-yu"; the Hall edition, following the Northern Supervisory, reads "Xuan-yi" (yi as righteousness).
s0214.idiomatic: On "chief administrator to the Xuan-yi Prince of Changsha": Ji reads Xuan-yu; Hall follows the Northern Supervisory with Xuan-yi (alternate graph).

s0215.literal: Comment: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian was made General of Resolute Declaration in the fourth year of Taijian; to write "Resolute Declaration" is correct.
s0215.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian became general of resolute declaration in Taijian year 4, so the title xuan-yi (resolute declaration) is correct.

s0216.literal: The Emperor ordered the responsible offices to investigate—"Emperor" was originally corrupted as "Zhang"; now corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and Yuan Gui 519.
s0216.idiomatic: On "the Emperor ordered inquiry": Di was written Zhang; emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and Yuan Gui 519.

s0217.literal: According to the auspicious section of the mountain-tomb ceremonial guard
s0217.idiomatic: According to the auspicious section of the imperial funeral procession regulations

s0219.literal: [Wu] within—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0219.idiomatic: On "[Wu] within": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and History of the Southern Dynasties.

s0220.literal: And extending to Martial Tiger Guard, drum-and-pipe, canopy-bearers, and chariot attendants—"Martial Tiger Guard" is "Tiger Brave Guard," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0220.idiomatic: On "and extending to martial tiger guard, drum-and-pipe, canopy-bearers, and chariot attendants": wu-ben renders hu-ben, taboo-changed for Tang.

s0223.literal: [ren] with mourning sash yet bearing the imperial canopy—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0223.idiomatic: On "[ren] with mourning sash yet bearing the imperial canopy": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and History of the Southern Dynasties.

s0224.literal: Curtained bier, spirit screen—"screen" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "chamber."
s0224.idiomatic: On "curtained bier, spirit screen": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read chamber for screen.

s0227.literal: Says: "'chamber' is a mistake for 'yi-back'; screen and yi-back are one thing.
s0227.idiomatic: writes: "Chamber is an error for yi; screen and yi are the same object.

s0228.literal: According to the text below there is the phrase "spirit yi-back before the cedar bier"; "screen" may originally have been "yi-back.""
s0228.idiomatic: Since the passage below has spirit yi before the cedar bier, ping (screen) may originally have been yi."

s0231.literal: [ji] Central Palace Attendant Zhu Tong, Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan—changed according to all editions.
s0231.idiomatic: On "[ji] and Central Palace Attendants Zhu Tong, Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan": emended per all editions.

s0232.literal: According to the old collation appended at the end of this scroll, it says
s0232.idiomatic: According to the old collation appended at the end of this scroll:

s0234.literal: "Kong Central Palace Attendant Zhu Tong" is doubtful; the edition seen by Zeng Gong and others likewise corrupted "ji" as "kong."
s0234.idiomatic: "Kong Central Palace Attendant Zhu Tong" is doubtful; the edition Zeng Gong and others saw also wrote kong for ji.

s0235.literal: Literary brush also then deployed its strength—"brush" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "ability/administer."
s0235.idiomatic: On "literary brush also then deployed its strength": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read gan (administer) for han (brush).
